sections.heading: Overshoot from RHPZ
sections.text: Cuk overshoot in CCM is the same mechanism as boost — the RHPZ limits voltage-loop bandwidth. Reduce kp to bring crossover below f_RHPZ/4. If the output is inverted, verify the feedback polarity is correct (negative feedback, not positive).

sections.heading: Slow settling from RHPZ limit
sections.text: If the Cuk settles slowly and gains are conservative, check the RHPZ frequency: f_RHPZ = (1-D)^2*R/(2*pi*L2). At high D and light load, this can be very low. Consider DCM operation or a different topology.

sections.heading: Excess ripple from coupling capacitor
sections.text: The coupling capacitor C1 carries the full input+output ripple current. Its ESR directly affects output ripple. Increase C1 or use a lower-ESR type (film or ceramic). Controller gain changes will not fix ripple dominated by passive component sizing.

sections.heading: Subharmonic oscillation
sections.text: If the Cuk shows period-doubling near fsw/2, this is subharmonic instability from peak-current-mode control. Add slope compensation with ramp >= (V_out)*D/(L2*fsw). This is an architecture fix, not a tuning fix.

sections.heading: Architecture limit
sections.text: If the Cuk fails across iterations due to RHPZ limitation or the inverted output creates control complexity, consider SEPIC (non-inverted output, same RHPZ behavior) or flyback (if isolation is needed).
